doc.title: Al Grey interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 3, 1995

title: Navy band dispute, Detroit, and meeting Benny Carter
summary: Band members complain about being put to labor, are shipped to Detroit, and Grey meets Benny Carter at the Paradise Theater.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: getting pretty good with the trombone. But then the sailors that we had in Hingham from being not able to read or write and like that, they were contained like in the department where they didn’t have no — to go out on liberty as it was called. See they had to stay there and so they got jealous of the band. See they can go out and everything, and would you believe they changed it around and wanted the band to go out there and do this work. And here the saxophone players with the fingers and everything, so we complained to the point writing a letter to the president and everything, telling them here we are, third class, second class and first class petty officers with our lyre up here for playing music, and here you’ve got us, we want to go out. And they said well they know too much, see? And they shipped our band out to Grosse Hill Naval Air Station in Detroit, outside of Detroit, Michigan. And from there I got out of the Navy. Benny Carter’s band came through town to play at the Paradise Theater which was the famous theater of Detroit at that time, which still, I think they’ve renovated it again. The Paradise Theater. And I went by to see Benny Carter, and they said, “Oh, we need a trombone player and I’ve been hearing about you around here playing at all the different clubs.”
So you were in the right place at the right time.
